chunks: It is narrated from Abū al-Maghrāʾ, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام said: “A woman who openly commits zinā should not be married, nor should a man who openly commits zinā be given in marriage, unless repentance is known from both of them.”

key_terms.التَّوْبَةُ: repentance that is recognized and known
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعْلِنَةُ: one who is openly public about the act

ai.seo_question: Can a person known to openly commit zinā be married in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning marriage with those who openly engage in zinā. It indicates that public persistence in such conduct is a barrier to marriage unless clear tawbah is known from the individuals involved.
